events_seen: TRADE (Jul 10): Adam receives Keaton Mitchell (RB, LAC). Wingard receives 2028 R3 pick.
WAIVER CLAIM (Jun 21): Drew added Colbie Young (WR, CIN) (dropped Joe Mixon (RB, FA)).
WAIVER CLAIM (Jun 08): Adam added Cyrus Allen (WR, KC) (dropped Phil Mafah (RB, DAL)).
WAIVER CLAIM (May 27): Charles added Chris Brooks (RB, GB) for $1 FAAB (dropped Austin Ekeler (RB, FA)).
WAIVER CLAIM (May 16): Charles added Matt Hibner (TE, BAL) (dropped Moliki Matavao (TE, NO)).
CUT (May 16): Charles released Zonovan Knight (RB, ARI).
WAIVER CLAIM (May 13): Shaq added Zavion Thomas (WR, CHI).
WAIVER CLAIM (May 12): Adam added John Michael Gyllenborg (TE, KC) (dropped Elijah Higgins (TE, ARI)).
CUT (May 11): Jake released Evan Hull (RB, HOU).
WAIVER CLAIM (May 11): Corbishley added Jam Miller (RB, NE).

tweets.name: Vance Hollis
tweets.text: Sovereign Draft Reserve is sitting on a pile of 2027 and 2028 capital and the stock is somehow not moving. The market is punishing Wingard for refusing to convert picks into production — and honestly? The market is right. Picks don't score points. At some point the shelf life on 'trust the process' expires.

tweets.name: Dina Ravioli
tweets.text: A few people have asked me about the Deepwater situation. I'm not hearing anything imminent on the trade front, but I am hearing that the people around Mitchum are increasingly frustrated. 'Board wants a buy/sell call' is the phrase I keep getting back. That's not nothing.

tweets.name: Bo Ruckman
tweets.text: Adam got Keaton Mitchell for a 2028 third-rounder and Wingard is out here acting like he won the trade. A THIRD. FROM 2028. Someone get me on a panel to discuss this because I have grievances.

tweets.name: Jay Kelpey
tweets.text: The Cyrus Allen add for Helix is getting zero attention and I think people are sleeping on it. Kansas City WR room, coaching staff that manufactures targets, and Adam already cleared the TE depth by grabbing Gyllenborg earlier in the window. He's been quietly building a full roster around that model. That's not waiver fishing — that's infrastructure.

tweets.name: Terrence E. Odom
tweets.text: I have been critical of Ryan. Publicly, repeatedly, on record. The $77.61 opening price was not an insult — it was the market doing its job. The market was wrong. I can say that. What I cannot say is that Ryan's process was sound, because it was not. He won anyway. Both things are true and I am deeply uncomfortable about it.

tweets.name: Matteo Honeydew
tweets.text: EchoPoint's RB room is elite and Jake still hasn't addressed TE — which in a TE premium league is like building a beautiful house and leaving the roof off. Great curb appeal. Structurally, you're one rainstorm from a disaster.

tweets.name: Clara Hopkins
tweets.text: Exchange Report is Thursday. Vivienne's already told me the Deepwater segment alone could run the whole hour if we let it. We won't. But it could.

tweets.name: Chad Bellwether
tweets.text: Colbie Young is actually a masterstroke by Drew and I'll tell you why: rebuilds require assets nobody else values yet. The fact that Atlas is at $44 is irrelevant. The market has always been afraid of innovation. Drew is innovating. Nobody panic.

tweets.name: Big Dog
tweets.text: Charles added a TE, added a running back, cut dead weight, and did it all so quietly that most of the league didn't notice. That's what a 23-5 operation looks like in the offseason. Crownline doesn't make noise. They make moves.
